# SMA-810: a tool result for the handoff transfer call

Linear: [SMA-810](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-810). Size: small change (short design).

## Intent

In a run with a handoff, the transfer tool call gets no tool result in the event stream.
`SessionRecorder::drain` then closes the call with a synthetic `ToolReturned` at the **end**
of the log, after all child events. When the session goes to a model again, the transfer
call and its result are far apart. Some providers require the result directly after the
call, and they reject the request.

SMA-803 adds a second effect. A provider can give the same call id to the transfer call
and to a deferred call of the child (the Gemini fallback id `fc_{n}`). The late transfer
result then closes the deferral, so SMA-803 denies such a deferral ("deferral not
possible: call id {id} repeats in this run"). When the transfer result comes directly
after the handoff, this deny is not necessary.

**Release state.** `paigasus-helikon-core` 0.6.0 is on crates.io (published 2026-11-20).
It contains SMA-803. So the deny and the old log layout (late transfer result) are
already in a release, and sessions with the old layout can exist.

## Goals

- G1. The parent emits a `ToolOutputItem` for each transfer call of the handoff response.
  The stored log of a handoff run is then:
  `[AssistantMessage]` `ToolCalled(t)` [`ToolCalled(u)` …] `HandoffOccurred`
  `ToolReturned(t)` [`ToolReturned(u)` …] … child events.
  `HandoffOccurred` projects to no item. So in the projected conversation the results come
  directly after the transfer calls of the same response, in call order.
- G2. Remove the SMA-803 deny for a repeated call id. A handoff child can defer a call
  that has the same call id as a transfer call above it, at any depth.
- G3. Tests check the adjacency on two levels:
  - **Stored log:** between a transfer `ToolCalled` and its `ToolReturned`, only
    `HandoffOccurred` and the other transfer calls and results of the same response occur.
  - **Projection:** every `ToolCall` has its `ToolResult` in the same contiguous tool
    block.

  Limit: under `ParallelAgent`, branch events interleave live (`workflow.rs`). The parent
  awaits `OnHandoff` between `ToolCallItem(t)` and `ToolOutputItem(t)`, so a sibling
  branch's items can be recorded between them. This is already true today for every tool
  call in a parallel branch. G3 applies to runs without `ParallelAgent`.

  Sven accepted on 2026-11-20 that "next to it" means next to it in the projected
  conversation (the model request), not in the raw log.
- G4. **Read-time repair of old sessions** (added at Gate 1 on Sven's request).
  `project()` moves the late result of each **transfer call** to directly after the
  transfer calls of its handoff response, and replaces the synthetic cancel text with
  the transfer text. A session stored before SMA-810 (any earlier core version) then
  projects as a new-layout session, with the exceptions listed in the G4 design. Every session backend (in-memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis) builds
  its snapshot with `core::project`, so the repair covers all of them. The stored log
  does not change. No other result moves.
- G5. **AG-UI call state and AG-UI id per call occurrence** (added at Gate 1
  on Sven's request). The AG-UI `EventMapper` keys `call_names`, `completed_calls` and
  `buffered_calls` by call id for the whole run. A provider that repeats call ids across
  model streams (Gemini `fc_{n}`) then gets a wrong tool name, a missing call, or merged
  arguments. Also, a client that keys on `toolCallId` merges two calls with one id. The
  mapper must give each call occurrence its own state and its own AG-UI id.

## Non-goals

- The stored log of an old session does not change. G4 repairs only the projection.
- The child transcript does not change. `thread_handoff_transcript` still drops all tool
  items, so the child never sees the transfer call or its result.
- Non-transfer calls in a handoff response stay out of scope. `transition()` drops them
  from the events, so the session does not record them. Their `ToolCallDelta`s can still
  reach AG-UI as START/ARGS with no result. This is not caused by this change.
- No change to the Temporal driver. It does not support handoffs.

## Anti-goals

- AG1. A "transferred" result for a handoff that did not occur. The result must come only
  after `OnHandoff` permits the handoff, the target agent is known, and the target run
  started.
- AG2. A change that breaks the resume of a session that core 0.6.0 stored (old layout).
- AG3. A second result for a transfer call (for example on a resumed run).

## Approaches

1. **Emit the result after `HandoffItem`, in the handoff arm of `agent.rs` (chosen).**
   The result comes after the `OnHandoff` veto, the depth check and the target lookup.
   `transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`) scans back from `HandoffOccurred` over
   `ToolCalled` and `AssistantMessage` only. A result after `HandoffOccurred` keeps this
   scan valid for old and new logs.
2. Emit the result in `transition()`. Pure and easy to unit-test, but it runs before the
   `OnHandoff` veto and the target check, and it puts the result before
   `HandoffOccurred`, which breaks `transfer_calls_before`. It also writes a result before
   a swarm can drop the handoff. Rejected.
3. Fix only `SessionRecorder` (write a result on `HandoffItem`). The live event stream
   keeps the orphan call, so AG-UI clients still see a call with no result. Rejected.

Sven chose approach 1 on 2026-11-20.

## Design

### Emission (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs`, `NextAction::Handoff` arm)

The event order of a successful handoff becomes:

1. `ToolCallItem` for each transfer call (from `transition()`, unchanged).
2. Depth check, target lookup, `OnHandoff` (unchanged). A failure ends the run as today.
3. `HandoffItem { from, to }` (unchanged).
4. `target_agent.run(child, input)` is awaited. This only builds the child stream; it
   yields no event. (Today this call comes after step 6. Moving it earlier changes no
   observable order, because it emits nothing.)
5. **New:** one `ToolOutputItem` per transfer call, in the order of the `ToolCallItem`
   events.
   - On `Ok`: the first transfer call (the call that names the target) gets
     `transferred to {target}`. Each other transfer call of the same response gets
     `transfer not performed: this response already transferred to {target}`.
   - On `Err`: every transfer call gets `transfer failed: {target} did not start`, and
     the run ends with `RunFailed` as today. The text does not include the error, because
     the result goes to a model and the error can hold internal detail.
6. `AgentUpdated { agent: target }` (on `Ok` only), then the child events.

The content of each result is one `ContentPart::Text`. The parent does not push the
results into its own `conversation`: after the handoff arm, the parent only re-yields
child events and returns, so that state is never read.

The transfer call ids are the ids that `agent.rs` already collects as
`transfer_call_ids` from the `ToolCallItem` events of the handoff transition.

The early exits in step 2 (depth exceeded, unknown target, `OnHandoff` deny) emit no
result. The run ends there with `RunFailed`, so the recorder's synthetic result is the
last event, directly after the call. This is the behaviour of today.

### Remove the repeated-id deny

- Delete the `open_call_ids` check in the `Authorization::Defer` arm (`agent.rs`).
- Delete `RunContext.open_call_ids`, `open_call_ids()`, `with_open_call_ids()` and their
  copies in `handoff_child` / `subagent_child` (`context.rs`). They are `pub(crate)` and
  have no other use, so this is not an API change. Delete the unit test
  `handoff_child_keeps_open_call_ids_and_subagent_child_clears_them`.
- `transfer_call_ids` stays: step 5 uses it.

### Read-time repair in `project()` (G4, `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs`)

The second spec challenge rejected a first version that moved every result to the end
of its "tool block". A tool-only model response makes no `AssistantMessage`
(`model.rs` `build_items`), so one block can hold several responses, and the OpenAI and
LiteLLM translators then still send an invalid request. That version also moved results
in `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids, where it could swap the content of two
results. This version moves **only transfer results**, to a fixed place.

**Step 1: find the transfer calls.** For each `HandoffOccurred` at index `k`, the
transfer calls are the `ToolCalled` events in the run of `ToolCalled` /
`AssistantMessage` events directly before `k`. This is the scan of
`transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`). The two places share only this boundary scan
in one private helper. (`transfer_calls_before` also counts `later_calls` with a forward
scan per call; `project()` must not call that part, or it becomes O(n × calls).)

Scope: step 1 is exact for **sequential** logs. In a sequential log the scan stops at
the resume block, at `UserMessageInjected`, at recorded input and at an earlier
`HandoffOccurred`, and `transition()` never records the non-transfer calls of a handoff
response. Two cases can put another call into the scanned run: a `ParallelAgent`
sibling's `ToolCalled` (the `OnHandoff` await is a yield point), and a run whose new
input ends with a `ToolCall` item. G4 does not support these cases (same limit as G3).

**Step 2: find the result of each transfer call** (one O(n) pass over the events). Keep
the list of open calls, each with a flag "transfer". A `ToolReturned` or `ToolDeferred`
with call id `x` closes:

1. the most recent open **non-transfer** call with id `x`, if one exists;
2. else the earliest open **transfer** call with id `x`.

Why: in the old layout a child call can repeat the transfer call id (Gemini `fc_0`).
The log is then `TC fc_0 (transfer)`, `HandoffOccurred`, `TC fc_0 (child)`,
`TR fc_0 (child)`, …, `TR fc_0 (late cancel)`. The rule gives the child's result to
the child's call and the late cancel to the transfer call. The rule changes nothing for
non-transfer calls, because non-transfer results do not move.

**Step 3: project as today, and keep the source.** `project()` keeps a parallel list
`sources` with the event index of each message. `Compacted` truncates `sources` with
`messages`. (A `Compacted` event counts **events**, so the repair must not reorder
events before projection: that would change which events a later `Compacted` removes.)

**Step 4: move, after projection.** For each handoff response whose transfer calls are
still in `messages`: the target position is directly after the last transfer call
message of that response. Each transfer result that is in `messages` but not at its
target moves there, in the order of its call. In one O(n) rebuild pass (no repeated
`Vec::remove`/`insert`):

- A result that is already at its target (the new layout) does not move.
- A result whose call was removed by `Compacted` stays where it is (today's behaviour).
- A result removed by `Compacted` while its call stays: the call keeps no result, as
  today.

**Step 5: correct the text of a moved late result.** If a moved result has exactly
the synthetic cancel text (`tool call did not complete (run cancelled/timed out)`), the
repair replaces it with the G1 text: `transferred to {to}` for the first transfer call
of the response (`to` comes from the `HandoffOccurred` event), and `transfer not
performed: this response already transferred to {to}` for each other call. Each level
uses the `to` of its own `HandoffOccurred`.

Why this is true: a result moves only when a recorded event lies between the transfer
call's handoff and the result. In a sequential log, such an event comes from the target
agent, so the target started and the transfer occurred. (`SequentialAgent` stops on a
failure; only `ParallelAgent` can break this, see the scope note in step 1.) When
`target_agent.run()` failed in the old code, the log is `TC t, HO, TR t(cancel)`: the
result is already at its target, so it does not move and keeps the cancel text.
Without this step, the model sees "did not complete" after a transfer that succeeded,
and it can call the transfer tool again. A result with any other text keeps its text.

The cancel text is one `const` in `session.rs`. `cancelled_result`, the repair and the
T7 helper all use it.

The repair is one named private function (for example
`repair_legacy_transfer_results`), so it is easy to find and to test. It has no removal
date: sessions stored before SMA-810 can live for a long time.

Exceptions (an old log does not give exactly the new layout):

- An old log where `target_agent.run()` failed keeps the cancel text. The new code
  writes `transfer failed: {target} did not start`.
- An old successful handoff whose child recorded no event at all keeps the cancel text
  (no event lies between, so the result does not move and is not rewritten). The model
  can still call the transfer tool again in this rare case.

Properties:

- A log that has no `HandoffOccurred`, and a new-layout log, project exactly as today.
  This includes `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids.
- The repair adds and removes no message, so the message count stays the same.
  (`CompactingSession` checks `len()`, which does not change. Step 5 changes the text
  length, so its token estimate can change slightly. Tests must not assert equal token
  counts before and after the repair.)
- After the repair, a transfer call and its result are adjacent in the sense of
  `close_open_transfers` (result directly after the transfer calls of its response). So
  FIFO (`paired_result`, `agent_view`) and the step 2 rule give the same pairs for
  transfer calls. `close_open_transfers` keeps its "move" branch as a defence for a
  custom `Session` that overrides `snapshot()` without `project()`.
- `agent_view` (`deferral.rs`) calls `project()` per log segment. A segment that does
  not contain the `HandoffOccurred` of a transfer call does not move that call's result.
  The child segment drops the leading transfer result as today (it closes no open call).
- `ResumePlan::from_events` never maps snapshot indices to event indices. The repair
  moves results only to earlier positions and never reorders `ToolCall` items, so
  `CallNotInHistory` and `nth(later_calls)` keep their answers.
- `project()` emits one `tracing::debug!` (target `paigasus::core::session`) with the
  number of moved results when the number is not zero.
- The rustdoc of `project` states the repair, and that the snapshot order no longer
  follows the event order one-to-one for old-layout handoff logs.

### AG-UI call state (G5, `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs`)

Two spec challenges shaped this section. The first showed that removing state at
`ToolOutputItem` is not enough, and that two spans with one `toolCallId` break the
mapper's own client contract ("one call id maps to exactly one span", module doc). The
second showed that a reset at `TurnStarted` makes `ParallelAgent` output worse for every
provider: a sibling branch's `TurnStarted` can arrive between a call's deltas and its
`ToolCallItem`, and a reset there splits one call into two or renders it as `"unknown"`.
So G5 has **no reset at `TurnStarted`**. It starts a new occurrence of a provider id
only when the events prove that a new call started.

**Call occurrences.** The mapper keys all per-call state (`call_names`,
`completed_calls`, `buffered_calls`, `open_call`) by the **AG-UI id** of the occurrence,
not by the provider id. It keeps:

- `current: HashMap<String, Occurrence>`: provider id → the latest occurrence (its
  AG-UI id, whether a name-carrying delta was seen, whether its `ToolCallItem` was seen).
- `used_ids: HashSet<String>`: every AG-UI id that the run already emitted.

A new occurrence of provider id `x` starts when:

1. a `ToolCallDelta` for `x` with `name: Some(..)` arrives, and the current occurrence
   of `x` already had a name-carrying delta (the core contract gives `name: Some`
   exactly once per call, `model.rs`; the mapper already relies on this);
2. a `ToolCallItem` for `x` arrives, and the current occurrence of `x` already had its
   `ToolCallItem` (a non-streamed call that reuses the id);
3. there is no current occurrence of `x`.

The AG-UI id of a new occurrence is `x` when `x` is not in `used_ids`. Otherwise it is
`x~n` with the smallest `n` ≥ 2 such that `x~n` is not in `used_ids` (so an alias never
equals a provider id that the run already emitted). Every frame for the call (`START`,
`ARGS`, `END`, `RESULT`) uses the AG-UI id.

**Results and approvals.** A `ToolOutputItem` for `x` uses the AG-UI id of the current
occurrence of `x`. A `helikon.approval` CUSTOM frame (`ApprovalRequested`) also maps its
`call_id` through the current occurrence, so a client can connect it to the span. A
result for an id with no occurrence (only possible under `ParallelAgent` or for a
resume-window result) uses the provider id, as today.

- A result for an occurrence that is still in `buffered_calls` (only possible under
  `ParallelAgent`) flushes that buffered call first, so its span gets its name.
- Sequential flows: a call's result always comes before the next `TurnStarted`
  (`loop_state.rs`), and the transfer result comes after `HandoffItem` and before the
  child's first `TurnStarted`. So the "current occurrence" of a result is its own call.
- `ParallelAgent` with unique provider ids (OpenAI, Anthropic): no rule above fires a
  second time, so the output is exactly as today.
- Limit: `ParallelAgent` branches that both use one provider id can still mix two calls.
  This is the same as today.
- Limit: AG-UI ids are unique **per run**. The mapper is new for each request
  (`agui/sse.rs`), so two runs in one AG-UI thread can both emit `fc_0`.
- The module doc, the field docs and the invariant "one `toolCallId` maps to exactly one
  span" stay. Update the docs for the occurrence rule.
- Core contract wording: provider call ids are unique **at item level** in one stream
  (the accumulator merges deltas by id; `model.rs`).

**Oracle `assert_tool_calls_well_formed`.** Check (3) today keys `received` on the
provider `call_id` and `emitted` on the AG-UI `toolCallId`, so it cannot hold when an id
repeats. Change it as follows, with a rule that does not copy the mapper's logic:

- Split `received` per occurrence by the fixture's own structure: in the sequential
  fixtures, cut at each `TurnStarted` and at each `HandoffItem`. Occurrence `n` of
  provider id `x` maps to `x` (n = 1) or `x~n`.
- Assert that the emitted args of each AG-UI id equal the received args of its
  occurrence.
- Assert that each `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` uses the AG-UI id of the call that its
  `ToolOutputItem` closes.

### Interaction checks (verified against the code by the spec challenge)

- **Resume.** A resumed run descends the handoff path with no `HandoffItem`
  (`agent.rs`, resume routing), so it emits no second transfer result.
- **`close_open_transfers`.** It finds each result with `paired_result` and moves it to
  directly after its call. With one transfer call this is no change. With two or more
  calls the projection `[TC t, TC u, TR t, TR u]` becomes `[TC t, TR t, TC u, TR u]` in
  the model request. Both forms are valid provider input, and SMA-803 does the same on
  old logs.
- **Child view.** `agent_view` drops a `ToolResult` that closes no open call. The new
  transfer result comes first in the child part of the log and the child view has no
  transfer call, so the view drops it.
- **Open deferrals.** `open_deferral_positions` treats a deferral as closed when a later
  `ToolReturned` has the same call id. In the old layout, the late transfer result came
  after the child's deferral with the same id, so the deferral was not open. This was the
  main reason for the deny. In the new layout the transfer result comes before the
  child's call, so the deferral stays open.
- **Resume validity.** `ResumePlan::from_events` finds the last `ToolCall` with the
  deferred call id and requires no later `ToolResult` with that id. The new layout
  passes this check too.
- **Three levels with one id.** The challenger traced `triage(fc_0) → budgeting(fc_0) →
  savings defers fc_0` through `open_deferral_positions`, `CallNotInHistory`,
  `transfer_calls_before` (`later_calls` 2 and 1), `agent_view`, `drain` and
  `close_open_transfers`. All are correct for the new layout. The safety now rests on a
  positional contract between the emission order in `agent.rs`, the scan in
  `transfer_calls_before`, and the `nth(later_calls)` search in `close_open_transfers`.
  Tests lock it (below).
- **Recorder.** The result arrives after the first `TurnStarted`, so it is outside the
  resume window and goes to the normal log.
- **Swarm.** When `max_handoffs` is exceeded, the swarm drops the child stream at the
  `HandoffItem`, before the new result is polled. The run fails, and the recorder's
  synthetic result is the last event, next to the call.
- **AG-UI.** `ToolOutputItem` maps to `TOOL_CALL_RESULT`. Clients now get a result for
  the transfer call.

1	# SMA-810: a tool result for the handoff transfer call
2	
3	Linear: [SMA-810](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-810). Size: small change (short design).
4	
5	## Intent
6	
7	In a run with a handoff, the transfer tool call gets no tool result in the event stream.
8	`SessionRecorder::drain` then closes the call with a synthetic `ToolReturned` at the **end**
9	of the log, after all child events. When the session goes to a model again, the transfer
10	call and its result are far apart. Some providers require the result directly after the
11	call, and they reject the request.
12	
13	SMA-803 adds a second effect. A provider can give the same call id to the transfer call
14	and to a deferred call of the child (the Gemini fallback id `fc_{n}`). The late transfer
15	result then closes the deferral, so SMA-803 denies such a deferral ("deferral not
16	possible: call id {id} repeats in this run"). When the transfer result comes directly
17	after the handoff, this deny is not necessary.
18	
19	**Release state.** `paigasus-helikon-core` 0.6.0 is on crates.io (published 2026-11-20).
20	It contains SMA-803. So the deny and the old log layout (late transfer result) are
21	already in a release, and sessions with the old layout can exist.
22	
23	## Goals
24	
25	- G1. The parent emits a `ToolOutputItem` for each transfer call of the handoff response.
26	  The stored log of a handoff run is then:
27	  `[AssistantMessage]` `ToolCalled(t)` [`ToolCalled(u)` …] `HandoffOccurred`
28	  `ToolReturned(t)` [`ToolReturned(u)` …] … child events.
29	  `HandoffOccurred` projects to no item. So in the projected conversation the results come
30	  directly after the transfer calls of the same response, in call order.
31	- G2. Remove the SMA-803 deny for a repeated call id. A handoff child can defer a call
32	  that has the same call id as a transfer call above it, at any depth.
33	- G3. Tests check the adjacency on two levels:
34	  - **Stored log:** between a transfer `ToolCalled` and its `ToolReturned`, only
35	    `HandoffOccurred` and the other transfer calls and results of the same response occur.
36	  - **Projection:** every `ToolCall` has its `ToolResult` in the same contiguous tool
37	    block.
38	
39	  Limit: under `ParallelAgent`, branch events interleave live (`workflow.rs`). The parent
40	  awaits `OnHandoff` between `ToolCallItem(t)` and `ToolOutputItem(t)`, so a sibling
41	  branch's items can be recorded between them. This is already true today for every tool
42	  call in a parallel branch. G3 applies to runs without `ParallelAgent`.
43	
44	  Sven accepted on 2026-11-20 that "next to it" means next to it in the projected
45	  conversation (the model request), not in the raw log.
46	- G4. **Read-time repair of old sessions** (added at Gate 1 on Sven's request).
47	  `project()` moves the late result of each **transfer call** to directly after the
48	  transfer calls of its handoff response, and replaces the synthetic cancel text with
49	  the transfer text. A session stored before SMA-810 (any earlier core version) then
50	  projects as a new-layout session, with the exceptions listed in the G4 design. Every session backend (in-memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis) builds
51	  its snapshot with `core::project`, so the repair covers all of them. The stored log
52	  does not change. No other result moves.
53	- G5. **AG-UI call state and AG-UI id per call occurrence** (added at Gate 1
54	  on Sven's request). The AG-UI `EventMapper` keys `call_names`, `completed_calls` and
55	  `buffered_calls` by call id for the whole run. A provider that repeats call ids across
56	  model streams (Gemini `fc_{n}`) then gets a wrong tool name, a missing call, or merged
57	  arguments. Also, a client that keys on `toolCallId` merges two calls with one id. The
58	  mapper must give each call occurrence its own state and its own AG-UI id.
59	
60	## Non-goals
61	
62	- The stored log of an old session does not change. G4 repairs only the projection.
63	- The child transcript does not change. `thread_handoff_transcript` still drops all tool
64	  items, so the child never sees the transfer call or its result.
65	- Non-transfer calls in a handoff response stay out of scope. `transition()` drops them
66	  from the events, so the session does not record them. Their `ToolCallDelta`s can still
67	  reach AG-UI as START/ARGS with no result. This is not caused by this change.
68	- No change to the Temporal driver. It does not support handoffs.
69	
70	## Anti-goals
71	
72	- AG1. A "transferred" result for a handoff that did not occur. The result must come only
73	  after `OnHandoff` permits the handoff, the target agent is known, and the target run
74	  started.
75	- AG2. A change that breaks the resume of a session that core 0.6.0 stored (old layout).
76	- AG3. A second result for a transfer call (for example on a resumed run).
77	
78	## Approaches
79	
80	1. **Emit the result after `HandoffItem`, in the handoff arm of `agent.rs` (chosen).**
81	   The result comes after the `OnHandoff` veto, the depth check and the target lookup.
82	   `transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`) scans back from `HandoffOccurred` over
83	   `ToolCalled` and `AssistantMessage` only. A result after `HandoffOccurred` keeps this
84	   scan valid for old and new logs.
85	2. Emit the result in `transition()`. Pure and easy to unit-test, but it runs before the
86	   `OnHandoff` veto and the target check, and it puts the result before
87	   `HandoffOccurred`, which breaks `transfer_calls_before`. It also writes a result before
88	   a swarm can drop the handoff. Rejected.
89	3. Fix only `SessionRecorder` (write a result on `HandoffItem`). The live event stream
90	   keeps the orphan call, so AG-UI clients still see a call with no result. Rejected.
91	
92	Sven chose approach 1 on 2026-11-20.
93	
94	## Design
95	
96	### Emission (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs`, `NextAction::Handoff` arm)
97	
98	The event order of a successful handoff becomes:
99	
100	1. `ToolCallItem` for each transfer call (from `transition()`, unchanged).
101	2. Depth check, target lookup, `OnHandoff` (unchanged). A failure ends the run as today.
102	3. `HandoffItem { from, to }` (unchanged).
103	4. `target_agent.run(child, input)` is awaited. This only builds the child stream; it
104	   yields no event. (Today this call comes after step 6. Moving it earlier changes no
105	   observable order, because it emits nothing.)
106	5. **New:** one `ToolOutputItem` per transfer call, in the order of the `ToolCallItem`
107	   events.
108	   - On `Ok`: the first transfer call (the call that names the target) gets
109	     `transferred to {target}`. Each other transfer call of the same response gets
110	     `transfer not performed: this response already transferred to {target}`.
111	   - On `Err`: every transfer call gets `transfer failed: {target} did not start`, and
112	     the run ends with `RunFailed` as today. The text does not include the error, because
113	     the result goes to a model and the error can hold internal detail.
114	6. `AgentUpdated { agent: target }` (on `Ok` only), then the child events.
115	
116	The content of each result is one `ContentPart::Text`. The parent does not push the
117	results into its own `conversation`: after the handoff arm, the parent only re-yields
118	child events and returns, so that state is never read.
119	
120	The transfer call ids are the ids that `agent.rs` already collects as
121	`transfer_call_ids` from the `ToolCallItem` events of the handoff transition.
122	
123	The early exits in step 2 (depth exceeded, unknown target, `OnHandoff` deny) emit no
124	result. The run ends there with `RunFailed`, so the recorder's synthetic result is the
125	last event, directly after the call. This is the behaviour of today.
126	
127	### Remove the repeated-id deny
128	
129	- Delete the `open_call_ids` check in the `Authorization::Defer` arm (`agent.rs`).
130	- Delete `RunContext.open_call_ids`, `open_call_ids()`, `with_open_call_ids()` and their
131	  copies in `handoff_child` / `subagent_child` (`context.rs`). They are `pub(crate)` and
132	  have no other use, so this is not an API change. Delete the unit test
133	  `handoff_child_keeps_open_call_ids_and_subagent_child_clears_them`.
134	- `transfer_call_ids` stays: step 5 uses it.
135	
136	### Read-time repair in `project()` (G4, `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs`)
137	
138	The second spec challenge rejected a first version that moved every result to the end
139	of its "tool block". A tool-only model response makes no `AssistantMessage`
140	(`model.rs` `build_items`), so one block can hold several responses, and the OpenAI and
141	LiteLLM translators then still send an invalid request. That version also moved results
142	in `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids, where it could swap the content of two
143	results. This version moves **only transfer results**, to a fixed place.
144	
145	**Step 1: find the transfer calls.** For each `HandoffOccurred` at index `k`, the
146	transfer calls are the `ToolCalled` events in the run of `ToolCalled` /
147	`AssistantMessage` events directly before `k`. This is the scan of
148	`transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`). The two places share only this boundary scan
149	in one private helper. (`transfer_calls_before` also counts `later_calls` with a forward
150	scan per call; `project()` must not call that part, or it becomes O(n × calls).)
151	
152	Scope: step 1 is exact for **sequential** logs. In a sequential log the scan stops at
153	the resume block, at `UserMessageInjected`, at recorded input and at an earlier
154	`HandoffOccurred`, and `transition()` never records the non-transfer calls of a handoff
155	response. Two cases can put another call into the scanned run: a `ParallelAgent`
156	sibling's `ToolCalled` (the `OnHandoff` await is a yield point), and a run whose new
157	input ends with a `ToolCall` item. G4 does not support these cases (same limit as G3).
158	
159	**Step 2: find the result of each transfer call** (one O(n) pass over the events). Keep
160	the list of open calls, each with a flag "transfer". A `ToolReturned` or `ToolDeferred`
161	with call id `x` closes:
162	
163	1. the most recent open **non-transfer** call with id `x`, if one exists;
164	2. else the earliest open **transfer** call with id `x`.
165	
166	Why: in the old layout a child call can repeat the transfer call id (Gemini `fc_0`).
167	The log is then `TC fc_0 (transfer)`, `HandoffOccurred`, `TC fc_0 (child)`,
168	`TR fc_0 (child)`, …, `TR fc_0 (late cancel)`. The rule gives the child's result to
169	the child's call and the late cancel to the transfer call. The rule changes nothing for
170	non-transfer calls, because non-transfer results do not move.
171	
172	**Step 3: project as today, and keep the source.** `project()` keeps a parallel list
173	`sources` with the event index of each message. `Compacted` truncates `sources` with
174	`messages`. (A `Compacted` event counts **events**, so the repair must not reorder
175	events before projection: that would change which events a later `Compacted` removes.)
176	
177	**Step 4: move, after projection.** For each handoff response whose transfer calls are
178	still in `messages`: the target position is directly after the last transfer call
179	message of that response. Each transfer result that is in `messages` but not at its
180	target moves there, in the order of its call. In one O(n) rebuild pass (no repeated
181	`Vec::remove`/`insert`):
182	
183	- A result that is already at its target (the new layout) does not move.
184	- A result whose call was removed by `Compacted` stays where it is (today's behaviour).
185	- A result removed by `Compacted` while its call stays: the call keeps no result, as
186	  today.
187	
188	**Step 5: correct the text of a moved late result.** If a moved result has exactly
189	the synthetic cancel text (`tool call did not complete (run cancelled/timed out)`), the
190	repair replaces it with the G1 text: `transferred to {to}` for the first transfer call
191	of the response (`to` comes from the `HandoffOccurred` event), and `transfer not
192	performed: this response already transferred to {to}` for each other call. Each level
193	uses the `to` of its own `HandoffOccurred`.
194	
195	Why this is true: a result moves only when a recorded event lies between the transfer
196	call's handoff and the result. In a sequential log, such an event comes from the target
197	agent, so the target started and the transfer occurred. (`SequentialAgent` stops on a
198	failure; only `ParallelAgent` can break this, see the scope note in step 1.) When
199	`target_agent.run()` failed in the old code, the log is `TC t, HO, TR t(cancel)`: the
200	result is already at its target, so it does not move and keeps the cancel text.
201	Without this step, the model sees "did not complete" after a transfer that succeeded,
202	and it can call the transfer tool again. A result with any other text keeps its text.
203	
204	The cancel text is one `const` in `session.rs`. `cancelled_result`, the repair and the
205	T7 helper all use it.
206	
207	The repair is one named private function (for example
208	`repair_legacy_transfer_results`), so it is easy to find and to test. It has no removal
209	date: sessions stored before SMA-810 can live for a long time.
210	
211	Exceptions (an old log does not give exactly the new layout):
212	
213	- An old log where `target_agent.run()` failed keeps the cancel text. The new code
214	  writes `transfer failed: {target} did not start`.
215	- An old successful handoff whose child recorded no event at all keeps the cancel text
216	  (no event lies between, so the result does not move and is not rewritten). The model
217	  can still call the transfer tool again in this rare case.
218	
219	Properties:
220	
221	- A log that has no `HandoffOccurred`, and a new-layout log, project exactly as today.
222	  This includes `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids.
223	- The repair adds and removes no message, so the message count stays the same.
224	  (`CompactingSession` checks `len()`, which does not change. Step 5 changes the text
225	  length, so its token estimate can change slightly. Tests must not assert equal token
226	  counts before and after the repair.)
227	- After the repair, a transfer call and its result are adjacent in the sense of
228	  `close_open_transfers` (result directly after the transfer calls of its response). So
229	  FIFO (`paired_result`, `agent_view`) and the step 2 rule give the same pairs for
230	  transfer calls. `close_open_transfers` keeps its "move" branch as a defence for a
231	  custom `Session` that overrides `snapshot()` without `project()`.
232	- `agent_view` (`deferral.rs`) calls `project()` per log segment. A segment that does
233	  not contain the `HandoffOccurred` of a transfer call does not move that call's result.
234	  The child segment drops the leading transfer result as today (it closes no open call).
235	- `ResumePlan::from_events` never maps snapshot indices to event indices. The repair
236	  moves results only to earlier positions and never reorders `ToolCall` items, so
237	  `CallNotInHistory` and `nth(later_calls)` keep their answers.
238	- `project()` emits one `tracing::debug!` (target `paigasus::core::session`) with the
239	  number of moved results when the number is not zero.
240	- The rustdoc of `project` states the repair, and that the snapshot order no longer
241	  follows the event order one-to-one for old-layout handoff logs.
242	
243	### AG-UI call state (G5, `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs`)
244	
245	Two spec challenges shaped this section. The first showed that removing state at
246	`ToolOutputItem` is not enough, and that two spans with one `toolCallId` break the
247	mapper's own client contract ("one call id maps to exactly one span", module doc). The
248	second showed that a reset at `TurnStarted` makes `ParallelAgent` output worse for every
249	provider: a sibling branch's `TurnStarted` can arrive between a call's deltas and its
250	`ToolCallItem`, and a reset there splits one call into two or renders it as `"unknown"`.
251	So G5 has **no reset at `TurnStarted`**. It starts a new occurrence of a provider id
252	only when the events prove that a new call started.
253	
254	**Call occurrences.** The mapper keys all per-call state (`call_names`,
255	`completed_calls`, `buffered_calls`, `open_call`) by the **AG-UI id** of the occurrence,
256	not by the provider id. It keeps:
257	
258	- `current: HashMap<String, Occurrence>`: provider id → the latest occurrence (its
259	  AG-UI id, whether a name-carrying delta was seen, whether its `ToolCallItem` was seen).
260	- `used_ids: HashSet<String>`: every AG-UI id that the run already emitted.
261	
262	A new occurrence of provider id `x` starts when:
263	
264	1. a `ToolCallDelta` for `x` with `name: Some(..)` arrives, and the current occurrence
265	   of `x` already had a name-carrying delta (the core contract gives `name: Some`
266	   exactly once per call, `model.rs`; the mapper already relies on this);
267	2. a `ToolCallItem` for `x` arrives, and the current occurrence of `x` already had its
268	   `ToolCallItem` (a non-streamed call that reuses the id);
269	3. there is no current occurrence of `x`.
270	
271	The AG-UI id of a new occurrence is `x` when `x` is not in `used_ids`. Otherwise it is
272	`x~n` with the smallest `n` ≥ 2 such that `x~n` is not in `used_ids` (so an alias never
273	equals a provider id that the run already emitted). Every frame for the call (`START`,
274	`ARGS`, `END`, `RESULT`) uses the AG-UI id.
275	
276	**Results and approvals.** A `ToolOutputItem` for `x` uses the AG-UI id of the current
277	occurrence of `x`. A `helikon.approval` CUSTOM frame (`ApprovalRequested`) also maps its
278	`call_id` through the current occurrence, so a client can connect it to the span. A
279	result for an id with no occurrence (only possible under `ParallelAgent` or for a
280	resume-window result) uses the provider id, as today.
281	
282	- A result for an occurrence that is still in `buffered_calls` (only possible under
283	  `ParallelAgent`) flushes that buffered call first, so its span gets its name.
284	- Sequential flows: a call's result always comes before the next `TurnStarted`
285	  (`loop_state.rs`), and the transfer result comes after `HandoffItem` and before the
286	  child's first `TurnStarted`. So the "current occurrence" of a result is its own call.
287	- `ParallelAgent` with unique provider ids (OpenAI, Anthropic): no rule above fires a
288	  second time, so the output is exactly as today.
289	- Limit: `ParallelAgent` branches that both use one provider id can still mix two calls.
290	  This is the same as today.
291	- Limit: AG-UI ids are unique **per run**. The mapper is new for each request
292	  (`agui/sse.rs`), so two runs in one AG-UI thread can both emit `fc_0`.
293	- The module doc, the field docs and the invariant "one `toolCallId` maps to exactly one
294	  span" stay. Update the docs for the occurrence rule.
295	- Core contract wording: provider call ids are unique **at item level** in one stream
296	  (the accumulator merges deltas by id; `model.rs`).
297	
298	**Oracle `assert_tool_calls_well_formed`.** Check (3) today keys `received` on the
299	provider `call_id` and `emitted` on the AG-UI `toolCallId`, so it cannot hold when an id
300	repeats. Change it as follows, with a rule that does not copy the mapper's logic:
301	
302	- Split `received` per occurrence by the fixture's own structure: in the sequential
303	  fixtures, cut at each `TurnStarted` and at each `HandoffItem`. Occurrence `n` of
304	  provider id `x` maps to `x` (n = 1) or `x~n`.
305	- Assert that the emitted args of each AG-UI id equal the received args of its
306	  occurrence.
307	- Assert that each `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` uses the AG-UI id of the call that its
308	  `ToolOutputItem` closes.
309	
310	### Wording updates
311	
312	Public text that documents the removed deny (must change):
313	
314	- `docs/book/src/concepts/permissions-guardrails-hooks.md` ("Repeated call ids"
315	  paragraph): say that the deferral works, and why.
316	- Rustdoc of `RunContext::with_deferred_tool_calls` (`context.rs`): remove the deny text.
317	
318	Public text on the handoff event order:
319	
320	- `docs/book/src/concepts/multi-agent-patterns.md` ("`HandoffItem` followed by
321	  `AgentUpdated`"): add the transfer results between them.
322	- `docs/book/src/concepts/agent-loop.md`: check it, and update it if it lists the order.
323	
324	Internal comments that say the recorder closes transfer calls at the end of the run, or
325	that the transfer calls get no result while the child runs:
326	
327	- `agent.rs` (comment at `transfer_call_ids`).
328	- `resume_exec.rs` (`close_open_transfers` doc).
329	- `deferral.rs` (`agent_view` doc; the comment in the
330	  `child_history_drops_the_recorder_result…` test).
331	- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/deferred_resume.rs` (the helper docs near
332	  `text_then_call_b_session`, `handoff_session_with`, and the comment near line 969).
333	
334	Each rewrite says that the parent emits the result after the handoff, and that a session
335	from core 0.6.0 can still hold a late result.
336	
337	### Interaction checks (verified against the code by the spec challenge)
338	
339	- **Resume.** A resumed run descends the handoff path with no `HandoffItem`
340	  (`agent.rs`, resume routing), so it emits no second transfer result.
341	- **`close_open_transfers`.** It finds each result with `paired_result` and moves it to
342	  directly after its call. With one transfer call this is no change. With two or more
343	  calls the projection `[TC t, TC u, TR t, TR u]` becomes `[TC t, TR t, TC u, TR u]` in
344	  the model request. Both forms are valid provider input, and SMA-803 does the same on
345	  old logs.
346	- **Child view.** `agent_view` drops a `ToolResult` that closes no open call. The new
347	  transfer result comes first in the child part of the log and the child view has no
348	  transfer call, so the view drops it.
349	- **Open deferrals.** `open_deferral_positions` treats a deferral as closed when a later
350	  `ToolReturned` has the same call id. In the old layout, the late transfer result came
351	  after the child's deferral with the same id, so the deferral was not open. This was the
352	  main reason for the deny. In the new layout the transfer result comes before the
353	  child's call, so the deferral stays open.
354	- **Resume validity.** `ResumePlan::from_events` finds the last `ToolCall` with the
355	  deferred call id and requires no later `ToolResult` with that id. The new layout
356	  passes this check too.
357	- **Three levels with one id.** The challenger traced `triage(fc_0) → budgeting(fc_0) →
358	  savings defers fc_0` through `open_deferral_positions`, `CallNotInHistory`,
359	  `transfer_calls_before` (`later_calls` 2 and 1), `agent_view`, `drain` and
360	  `close_open_transfers`. All are correct for the new layout. The safety now rests on a
361	  positional contract between the emission order in `agent.rs`, the scan in
362	  `transfer_calls_before`, and the `nth(later_calls)` search in `close_open_transfers`.
363	  Tests lock it (below).
364	- **Recorder.** The result arrives after the first `TurnStarted`, so it is outside the
365	  resume window and goes to the normal log.
366	- **Swarm.** When `max_handoffs` is exceeded, the swarm drops the child stream at the
367	  `HandoffItem`, before the new result is polled. The run fails, and the recorder's
368	  synthetic result is the last event, next to the call.
369	- **AG-UI.** `ToolOutputItem` maps to `TOOL_CALL_RESULT`. Clients now get a result for
370	  the transfer call.
371	
372	## Tests
373	
374	Core integration (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/`), each with a session recorder:
375	
376	- T1. One handoff: the event order is `ToolCallItem(t)`, `HandoffItem`,
377	  `ToolOutputItem(t, "transferred to budgeting")`, `AgentUpdated`. The drained log has
378	  `ToolReturned(t)` directly after `HandoffOccurred` and no synthetic "did not complete"
379	  result. The G3 checks pass on the log and on the projection.
380	- T2. A response with two transfer calls gets two results, in call order, with the two
381	  texts above.
382	- T3. No result for a handoff that did not occur (AG1): an `OnHandoff` deny, the depth
383	  limit, an unknown target, and a swarm with `max_handoffs(0)`. In each case there is no
384	  `ToolOutputItem` for the transfer call and no "transferred" text. The swarm log is
385	  `[user, tool_called(call-1), tool_returned(call-1, CANCELLED)]` with no `handoff`.
386	- T4. A target whose `run` returns `Err`: the result is `transfer failed: {target} did
387	  not start`, then `RunFailed`.
388	- T5. No second result on a resume (AG3): extend
389	  `handoff_resume_runs_the_call_on_the_child_with_the_child_conversation` with "no

391	  cover the resume-route exits (depth limit, target `run` error) on a new-layout log:
392	  they emit no new `t1` result.
393	- T6. Three levels with one id (G2): `triage(fc_0) → budgeting(fc_0) → savings` defers

395	  - (a) The run defers. The labels are `tool_called(fc_0), handoff,
396	    tool_returned(fc_0, transferred to budgeting), tool_called(fc_0), handoff,
397	    tool_returned(fc_0, transferred to savings), tool_called(fc_0), tool_deferred(fc_0)`,
398	    with no cancel result.
399	  - (b) A resume runs the call, and `assert_tool_calls_paired` holds on every request.

402	- T7. Old layout (AG2): a test helper `with_late_transfer_results(session)` turns a

470	  - An alias never equals an emitted provider id: a run that emits `x~2` as a real

475	Runtime-tokio (`crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs`):
476	
477	- Change `deferral_with_the_call_id_of_an_open_transfer_call_is_denied` to assert that

481	## Release and docs
482	
483	- Commit types: `fix(core)` for G1 to G4, `fix(runtime-agentcore)` for G5 (separate
484	  commits on the branch). The `fix(core)` body names the three behaviour changes: (1) a

496	  only after SMA-819 is merged (both then go out in the same or a later release PR). The
497	  PR body states this.
498	- mdBook and rustdoc: see "Wording updates". Also check `docs/book/src/concepts/sessions.md`
499	  (or the page that describes `project`/snapshots) and add one sentence on the repair.
500	- Crate READMEs: no public API change, so no README edit.
501	
502	## Left to the builder
503	
504	- The exact test file and helper names.
505	- Whether the result texts come from a small private function in `agent.rs`.
506	
507	## Follow-up candidates (not in this change)
508	
509	- The read-time repair (G4) and the AG-UI call state (G5) were folded in at Gate 1.
510	- **Provider translators.** The second spec challenge found two
511	  translator bugs that this change does not cause:
512	  - Anthropic (`providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs`): for the items
513	    `[User, ToolCall, ToolResult, AssistantMessage]` the `AssistantMessage` arm flushes the
514	    pending `tool_result` before the pending `tool_use`. The wire becomes `user,
515	    user[tool_result], assistant[tool_use], assistant[text]`. Confirmed by reading the
516	    code. This shape occurs on every later run of a session after a tool-only response.
517	    **Decision (Sven, 2026-11-20):** this goes into SMA-819 (Anthropic translator, in
518	    progress). The SMA-819 session confirmed that SMA-819 already covers all three shapes,
519	    with unit tests and a live check against the Anthropic API. SMA-810 needs no change.
520	  - Gemini (`providers-gemini/src/translate/request.rs`): the `functionResponse` name is
521	    found by call id, and the last call with that id wins. With a repeated `fc_0`, an
522	    earlier result gets a later call's tool name.
523	    **Decision (Sven, 2026-11-20):** added to SMA-820 as part 2 (same Gemini file).
524	    SMA-810 needs no change for this.

# SMA-810: a tool result for the handoff transfer call

Linear: [SMA-810](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-810). Size: small change (short design).

## Intent

In a run with a handoff, the transfer tool call gets no tool result in the event stream.
`SessionRecorder::drain` then closes the call with a synthetic `ToolReturned` at the **end**
of the log, after all child events. When the session goes to a model again, the transfer
call and its result are far apart. Some providers require the result directly after the
call, and they reject the request.

SMA-803 adds a second effect. A provider can give the same call id to the transfer call
and to a deferred call of the child (the Gemini fallback id `fc_{n}`). The late transfer
result then closes the deferral, so SMA-803 denies such a deferral ("deferral not
possible: call id {id} repeats in this run"). When the transfer result comes directly
after the handoff, this deny is not necessary.

**Release state.** `paigasus-helikon-core` 0.6.0 is on crates.io (published 2026-11-20).
It contains SMA-803. So the deny and the old log layout (late transfer result) are
already in a release, and sessions with the old layout can exist.

## Goals

- G1. The parent emits a `ToolOutputItem` for each transfer call of the handoff response.
  The stored log of a handoff run is then:
  `[AssistantMessage]` `ToolCalled(t)` [`ToolCalled(u)` …] `HandoffOccurred`
  `ToolReturned(t)` [`ToolReturned(u)` …] … child events.
  `HandoffOccurred` projects to no item. So in the projected conversation the results come
  directly after the transfer calls of the same response, in call order.
- G2. Remove the SMA-803 deny for a repeated call id. A handoff child can defer a call
  that has the same call id as a transfer call above it, at any depth.
- G3. Tests check the adjacency on two levels:
  - **Stored log:** between a transfer `ToolCalled` and its `ToolReturned`, only
    `HandoffOccurred` and the other transfer calls and results of the same response occur.
  - **Projection:** every `ToolCall` has its `ToolResult` in the same contiguous tool
    block.

  Limit: under `ParallelAgent`, branch events interleave live (`workflow.rs`). The parent
  awaits `OnHandoff` between `ToolCallItem(t)` and `ToolOutputItem(t)`, so a sibling
  branch's items can be recorded between them. This is already true today for every tool
  call in a parallel branch. G3 applies to runs without `ParallelAgent`.

  Sven accepted on 2026-11-20 that "next to it" means next to it in the projected
  conversation (the model request), not in the raw log.
- G4. **Read-time repair of old sessions** (added at Gate 1 on Sven's request).
  `project()` moves the late result of each **transfer call** to directly after the
  transfer calls of its handoff response, and replaces the synthetic cancel text with
  the transfer text. A session stored before SMA-810 (any earlier core version) then
  projects as a new-layout session, with the exceptions listed in the G4 design. Every session backend (in-memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis) builds
  its snapshot with `core::project`, so the repair covers all of them. The stored log
  does not change. No other result moves.
- G5. **AG-UI call state and AG-UI id per call occurrence** (added at Gate 1
  on Sven's request). The AG-UI `EventMapper` keys `call_names`, `completed_calls` and
  `buffered_calls` by call id for the whole run. A provider that repeats call ids across
  model streams (Gemini `fc_{n}`) then gets a wrong tool name, a missing call, or merged
  arguments. Also, a client that keys on `toolCallId` merges two calls with one id. The
  mapper must give each call occurrence its own state and its own AG-UI id.

## Non-goals

- The stored log of an old session does not change. G4 repairs only the projection.
- The child transcript does not change. `thread_handoff_transcript` still drops all tool
  items, so the child never sees the transfer call or its result.
- Non-transfer calls in a handoff response stay out of scope. `transition()` drops them
  from the events, so the session does not record them. Their `ToolCallDelta`s can still
  reach AG-UI as START/ARGS with no result. This is not caused by this change.
- No change to the Temporal driver. It does not support handoffs.

## Anti-goals

- AG1. A "transferred" result for a handoff that did not occur. The result must come only
  after `OnHandoff` permits the handoff, the target agent is known, and the target run
  started.
- AG2. A change that breaks the resume of a session that core 0.6.0 stored (old layout).
- AG3. A second result for a transfer call (for example on a resumed run).

## Approaches

1. **Emit the result after `HandoffItem`, in the handoff arm of `agent.rs` (chosen).**
   The result comes after the `OnHandoff` veto, the depth check and the target lookup.
   `transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`) scans back from `HandoffOccurred` over
   `ToolCalled` and `AssistantMessage` only. A result after `HandoffOccurred` keeps this
   scan valid for old and new logs.
2. Emit the result in `transition()`. Pure and easy to unit-test, but it runs before the
   `OnHandoff` veto and the target check, and it puts the result before
   `HandoffOccurred`, which breaks `transfer_calls_before`. It also writes a result before
   a swarm can drop the handoff. Rejected.
3. Fix only `SessionRecorder` (write a result on `HandoffItem`). The live event stream
   keeps the orphan call, so AG-UI clients still see a call with no result. Rejected.

Sven chose approach 1 on 2026-11-20.

## Design

### Emission (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs`, `NextAction::Handoff` arm)

The event order of a successful handoff becomes:

1. `ToolCallItem` for each transfer call (from `transition()`, unchanged).
2. Depth check, target lookup, `OnHandoff` (unchanged). A failure ends the run as today.
3. `HandoffItem { from, to }` (unchanged).
4. `target_agent.run(child, input)` is awaited. This only builds the child stream; it
   yields no event. (Today this call comes after step 6. Moving it earlier changes no
   observable order, because it emits nothing.)
5. **New:** one `ToolOutputItem` per transfer call, in the order of the `ToolCallItem`
   events.
   - On `Ok`: the first transfer call (the call that names the target) gets
     `transferred to {target}`. Each other transfer call of the same response gets
     `transfer not performed: this response already transferred to {target}`.
   - On `Err`: every transfer call gets `transfer failed: {target} did not start`, and
     the run ends with `RunFailed` as today. The text does not include the error, because
     the result goes to a model and the error can hold internal detail.
6. `AgentUpdated { agent: target }` (on `Ok` only), then the child events.

The content of each result is one `ContentPart::Text`. The parent does not push the
results into its own `conversation`: after the handoff arm, the parent only re-yields
child events and returns, so that state is never read.

The transfer call ids are the ids that `agent.rs` already collects as
`transfer_call_ids` from the `ToolCallItem` events of the handoff transition.

The early exits in step 2 (depth exceeded, unknown target, `OnHandoff` deny) emit no
result. The run ends there with `RunFailed`, so the recorder's synthetic result is the
last event, directly after the call. This is the behaviour of today.

### Remove the repeated-id deny

- Delete the `open_call_ids` check in the `Authorization::Defer` arm (`agent.rs`).
- Delete `RunContext.open_call_ids`, `open_call_ids()`, `with_open_call_ids()` and their
  copies in `handoff_child` / `subagent_child` (`context.rs`). They are `pub(crate)` and
  have no other use, so this is not an API change. Delete the unit test
  `handoff_child_keeps_open_call_ids_and_subagent_child_clears_them`.
- `transfer_call_ids` stays: step 5 uses it.

### Read-time repair in `project()` (G4, `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs`)

The second spec challenge rejected a first version that moved every result to the end
of its "tool block". A tool-only model response makes no `AssistantMessage`
(`model.rs` `build_items`), so one block can hold several responses, and the OpenAI and
LiteLLM translators then still send an invalid request. That version also moved results
in `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids, where it could swap the content of two
results. This version moves **only transfer results**, to a fixed place.

**Step 1: find the transfer calls.** For each `HandoffOccurred` at index `k`, the
transfer calls are the `ToolCalled` events in the run of `ToolCalled` /
`AssistantMessage` events directly before `k`. This is the scan of
`transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`). The two places share only this boundary scan
in one private helper. (`transfer_calls_before` also counts `later_calls` with a forward
scan per call; `project()` must not call that part, or it becomes O(n × calls).)

Scope: step 1 is exact for **sequential** logs. In a sequential log the scan stops at
the resume block, at `UserMessageInjected`, at recorded input and at an earlier
`HandoffOccurred`, and `transition()` never records the non-transfer calls of a handoff
response. Two cases can put another call into the scanned run: a `ParallelAgent`
sibling's `ToolCalled` (the `OnHandoff` await is a yield point), and a run whose new
input ends with a `ToolCall` item. G4 does not support these cases (same limit as G3).

**Step 2: find the result of each transfer call** (one O(n) pass over the events). Keep
the list of open calls, each with a flag "transfer". A `ToolReturned` or `ToolDeferred`
with call id `x` closes:

1. the most recent open **non-transfer** call with id `x`, if one exists;
2. else the earliest open **transfer** call with id `x`.

Why: in the old layout a child call can repeat the transfer call id (Gemini `fc_0`).
The log is then `TC fc_0 (transfer)`, `HandoffOccurred`, `TC fc_0 (child)`,
`TR fc_0 (child)`, …, `TR fc_0 (late cancel)`. The rule gives the child's result to
the child's call and the late cancel to the transfer call. The rule changes nothing for
non-transfer calls, because non-transfer results do not move.

**Step 3: project as today, and keep the source.** `project()` keeps a parallel list
`sources` with the event index of each message. `Compacted` truncates `sources` with
`messages`. (A `Compacted` event counts **events**, so the repair must not reorder
events before projection: that would change which events a later `Compacted` removes.)

**Step 4: move, after projection.** For each handoff response whose transfer calls are
still in `messages`: the target position is directly after the last transfer call
message of that response. Each transfer result that is in `messages` but not at its
target moves there, in the order of its call. In one O(n) rebuild pass (no repeated
`Vec::remove`/`insert`):

- A result that is already at its target (the new layout) does not move.
- A result whose call was removed by `Compacted` stays where it is (today's behaviour).
- A result removed by `Compacted` while its call stays: the call keeps no result, as
  today.

**Step 5: correct the text of a moved late result.** If a moved result has exactly
the synthetic cancel text (`tool call did not complete (run cancelled/timed out)`), the
repair replaces it with the G1 text: `transferred to {to}` for the first transfer call
of the response (`to` comes from the `HandoffOccurred` event), and `transfer not
performed: this response already transferred to {to}` for each other call. Each level
uses the `to` of its own `HandoffOccurred`.

Why this is true: a result moves only when a recorded event lies between the transfer
call's handoff and the result. In a sequential log, such an event comes from the target
agent, so the target started and the transfer occurred. (`SequentialAgent` stops on a
failure; only `ParallelAgent` can break this, see the scope note in step 1.) When
`target_agent.run()` failed in the old code, the log is `TC t, HO, TR t(cancel)`: the
result is already at its target, so it does not move and keeps the cancel text.
Without this step, the model sees "did not complete" after a transfer that succeeded,
and it can call the transfer tool again. A result with any other text keeps its text.

The cancel text is one `const` in `session.rs`. `cancelled_result`, the repair and the
T7 helper all use it.

The repair is one named private function (for example
`repair_legacy_transfer_results`), so it is easy to find and to test. It has no removal
date: sessions stored before SMA-810 can live for a long time.

Exceptions (an old log does not give exactly the new layout):

- An old log where `target_agent.run()` failed keeps the cancel text. The new code
  writes `transfer failed: {target} did not start`.
- An old successful handoff whose child recorded no event at all keeps the cancel text
  (no event lies between, so the result does not move and is not rewritten). The model
  can still call the transfer tool again in this rare case.

Properties:

- A log that has no `HandoffOccurred`, and a new-layout log, project exactly as today.
  This includes `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids.
- The repair adds and removes no message, so the message count stays the same.
  (`CompactingSession` checks `len()`, which does not change. Step 5 changes the text
  length, so its token estimate can change slightly. Tests must not assert equal token
  counts before and after the repair.)
- After the repair, a transfer call and its result are adjacent in the sense of
  `close_open_transfers` (result directly after the transfer calls of its response). So
  FIFO (`paired_result`, `agent_view`) and the step 2 rule give the same pairs for
  transfer calls. `close_open_transfers` keeps its "move" branch as a defence for a
  custom `Session` that overrides `snapshot()` without `project()`.
- `agent_view` (`deferral.rs`) calls `project()` per log segment. A segment that does
  not contain the `HandoffOccurred` of a transfer call does not move that call's result.
  The child segment drops the leading transfer result as today (it closes no open call).
- `ResumePlan::from_events` never maps snapshot indices to event indices. The repair
  moves results only to earlier positions and never reorders `ToolCall` items, so
  `CallNotInHistory` and `nth(later_calls)` keep their answers.
- `project()` emits one `tracing::debug!` (target `paigasus::core::session`) with the
  number of moved results when the number is not zero.
- The rustdoc of `project` states the repair, and that the snapshot order no longer
  follows the event order one-to-one for old-layout handoff logs.

### AG-UI call state (G5, `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs`)

Two spec challenges shaped this section. The first showed that removing state at
`ToolOutputItem` is not enough, and that two spans with one `toolCallId` break the
mapper's own client contract ("one call id maps to exactly one span", module doc). The
second showed that a reset at `TurnStarted` makes `ParallelAgent` output worse for every
provider: a sibling branch's `TurnStarted` can arrive between a call's deltas and its
`ToolCallItem`, and a reset there splits one call into two or renders it as `"unknown"`.
So G5 has **no reset at `TurnStarted`**. It starts a new occurrence of a provider id
only when the events prove that a new call started.

**Call occurrences.** The mapper keys all per-call state (`call_names`,
`completed_calls`, `buffered_calls`, `open_call`) by the **AG-UI id** of the occurrence,
not by the provider id. It keeps:

- `current: HashMap<String, Occurrence>`: provider id → the latest occurrence (its
  AG-UI id, whether a name-carrying delta was seen, whether its `ToolCallItem` was seen).
- `used_ids: HashSet<String>`: every AG-UI id that the run already emitted.

A new occurrence of provider id `x` starts when:

1. a `ToolCallDelta` for `x` with `name: Some(..)` arrives, and the current occurrence
   of `x` already had a name-carrying delta (the core contract gives `name: Some`
   exactly once per call, `model.rs`; the mapper already relies on this);
2. a `ToolCallItem` for `x` arrives, and the current occurrence of `x` already had its
   `ToolCallItem` (a non-streamed call that reuses the id);
3. there is no current occurrence of `x`.

The AG-UI id of a new occurrence is `x` when `x` is not in `used_ids`. Otherwise it is
`x~n` with the smallest `n` ≥ 2 such that `x~n` is not in `used_ids` (so an alias never
equals a provider id that the run already emitted). Every frame for the call (`START`,
`ARGS`, `END`, `RESULT`) uses the AG-UI id.

**Results and approvals.** A `ToolOutputItem` for `x` uses the AG-UI id of the current
occurrence of `x`. A `helikon.approval` CUSTOM frame (`ApprovalRequested`) also maps its
`call_id` through the current occurrence, so a client can connect it to the span. A
result for an id with no occurrence (only possible under `ParallelAgent` or for a
resume-window result) uses the provider id, as today.

- A result for an occurrence that is still in `buffered_calls` (only possible under
  `ParallelAgent`) flushes that buffered call first, so its span gets its name.
- Sequential flows: a call's result always comes before the next `TurnStarted`
  (`loop_state.rs`), and the transfer result comes after `HandoffItem` and before the
  child's first `TurnStarted`. So the "current occurrence" of a result is its own call.
- `ParallelAgent` with unique provider ids (OpenAI, Anthropic): no rule above fires a
  second time, so the output is exactly as today.
- Limit: `ParallelAgent` branches that both use one provider id can still mix two calls.
  This is the same as today.
- Limit: AG-UI ids are unique **per run**. The mapper is new for each request
  (`agui/sse.rs`), so two runs in one AG-UI thread can both emit `fc_0`.
- The module doc, the field docs and the invariant "one `toolCallId` maps to exactly one
  span" stay. Update the docs for the occurrence rule.
- Core contract wording: provider call ids are unique **at item level** in one stream
  (the accumulator merges deltas by id; `model.rs`).

**Oracle `assert_tool_calls_well_formed`.** Check (3) today keys `received` on the
provider `call_id` and `emitted` on the AG-UI `toolCallId`, so it cannot hold when an id
repeats. Change it as follows, with a rule that does not copy the mapper's logic:

- Split `received` per occurrence by the fixture's own structure: in the sequential
  fixtures, cut at each `TurnStarted` and at each `HandoffItem`. Occurrence `n` of
  provider id `x` maps to `x` (n = 1) or `x~n`.
- Assert that the emitted args of each AG-UI id equal the received args of its
  occurrence.
- Assert that each `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` uses the AG-UI id of the call that its
  `ToolOutputItem` closes.

### Interaction checks (verified against the code by the spec challenge)

- **Resume.** A resumed run descends the handoff path with no `HandoffItem`
  (`agent.rs`, resume routing), so it emits no second transfer result.
- **`close_open_transfers`.** It finds each result with `paired_result` and moves it to
  directly after its call. With one transfer call this is no change. With two or more
  calls the projection `[TC t, TC u, TR t, TR u]` becomes `[TC t, TR t, TC u, TR u]` in
  the model request. Both forms are valid provider input, and SMA-803 does the same on
  old logs.
- **Child view.** `agent_view` drops a `ToolResult` that closes no open call. The new
  transfer result comes first in the child part of the log and the child view has no
  transfer call, so the view drops it.
- **Open deferrals.** `open_deferral_positions` treats a deferral as closed when a later
  `ToolReturned` has the same call id. In the old layout, the late transfer result came
  after the child's deferral with the same id, so the deferral was not open. This was the
  main reason for the deny. In the new layout the transfer result comes before the
  child's call, so the deferral stays open.
- **Resume validity.** `ResumePlan::from_events` finds the last `ToolCall` with the
  deferred call id and requires no later `ToolResult` with that id. The new layout
  passes this check too.
- **Three levels with one id.** The challenger traced `triage(fc_0) → budgeting(fc_0) →
  savings defers fc_0` through `open_deferral_positions`, `CallNotInHistory`,
  `transfer_calls_before` (`later_calls` 2 and 1), `agent_view`, `drain` and
  `close_open_transfers`. All are correct for the new layout. The safety now rests on a
  positional contract between the emission order in `agent.rs`, the scan in
  `transfer_calls_before`, and the `nth(later_calls)` search in `close_open_transfers`.
  Tests lock it (below).
- **Recorder.** The result arrives after the first `TurnStarted`, so it is outside the
  resume window and goes to the normal log.
- **Swarm.** When `max_handoffs` is exceeded, the swarm drops the child stream at the
  `HandoffItem`, before the new result is polled. The run fails, and the recorder's
  synthetic result is the last event, next to the call.
- **AG-UI.** `ToolOutputItem` maps to `TOOL_CALL_RESULT`. Clients now get a result for
  the transfer call.

  - Handoff: the parent's turn 1 uses `fc_1` for a normal call; the handoff response is
    `[search fc_0, transfer fc_1]` (only the transfer gets a `ToolCallItem`). So the
    transfer call is the second use of `fc_1` (`fc_1~2`), and its result after
    `HandoffItem` uses `fc_1~2`. The child response `[lookup fc_0, pay fc_1]` renders
    each call with its own name and a fresh AG-UI id, and no args merge.
  - The same handoff with the transfer delta streamed first, so `search` is buffered.
  - `ParallelAgent` with unique ids: branch B's `TurnStarted` arrives between branch A's
    deltas and A's `ToolCallItem`. The output is exactly as today (one span, the right
    name, no second span).
  - An alias never equals an emitted provider id: a run that emits `x~2` as a real
    provider id and then reuses `x` gets `x~3`.
  - `ApprovalRequested` for a reused id carries the AG-UI id of the current occurrence.
  - The changed `assert_tool_calls_well_formed` (see G5) holds on every case.

Runtime-tokio (`crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs`):

- Change `deferral_with_the_call_id_of_an_open_transfer_call_is_denied` to assert that
  the child's `fc_0` call now defers, and that a resume of that deferral runs the call.
  Keep `assert_tool_calls_paired` on every child request. Rename the test to match.

## Release and docs

- Commit types: `fix(core)` for G1 to G4, `fix(runtime-agentcore)` for G5 (separate
  commits on the branch). The `fix(core)` body names the three behaviour changes: (1) a
  handoff run now emits a `ToolOutputItem` for each transfer call, (2) a deferral with a
  call id that repeats a transfer call id is no longer denied, and (3) `project()` moves
  the late result of a transfer call in a session stored before SMA-810 to directly
  after the call, with the transfer text. release-plz writes the CHANGELOG from
  the commits.
- **Release order (Anthropic).** The Anthropic translator sends `tool_result` before
  `tool_use` for `[User, TC, TR, AM]` until SMA-819 ships. The old layout projects to
  `user, TC t, AM(child), TR t`; the SMA-819 session found that the Anthropic API merges
  adjacent same-role turns, so that old shape is probably accepted. After G1 and G4 the
  projection is `user, TC t, TR t, AM(child)`, which the unfixed translator sends in the
  wrong order. So SMA-810 must not reach crates.io before SMA-819: merge the SMA-810 PR
  only after SMA-819 is merged (both then go out in the same or a later release PR). The
  PR body states this.
- mdBook and rustdoc: see "Wording updates". Also check `docs/book/src/concepts/sessions.md`
  (or the page that describes `project`/snapshots) and add one sentence on the repair.
- Crate READMEs: no public API change, so no README edit.

## Left to the builder

- The exact test file and helper names.
- Whether the result texts come from a small private function in `agent.rs`.

## Follow-up candidates (not in this change)

- The read-time repair (G4) and the AG-UI call state (G5) were folded in at Gate 1.
- **Provider translators.** The second spec challenge found two
  translator bugs that this change does not cause:
  - Anthropic (`providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs`): for the items
    `[User, ToolCall, ToolResult, AssistantMessage]` the `AssistantMessage` arm flushes the
    pending `tool_result` before the pending `tool_use`. The wire becomes `user,
    user[tool_result], assistant[tool_use], assistant[text]`. Confirmed by reading the
    code. This shape occurs on every later run of a session after a tool-only response.
    **Decision (Sven, 2026-11-20):** this goes into SMA-819 (Anthropic translator, in
    progress). The SMA-819 session confirmed that SMA-819 already covers all three shapes,
    with unit tests and a live check against the Anthropic API. SMA-810 needs no change.
  - Gemini (`providers-gemini/src/translate/request.rs`): the `functionResponse` name is
    found by call id, and the last call with that id wins. With a repeated `fc_0`, an
    earlier result gets a later call's tool name.
    **Decision (Sven, 2026-11-20):** added to SMA-820 as part 2 (same Gemini file).
    SMA-810 needs no change for this.

+When a handoff fires, the stream emits a `HandoffItem { from, to }`. Then it emits one

--- 6c1d9d33 fix(core): SMA-810 repair late transfer results when a session is projected
Behaviour change (3): project() moves the late result of each handoff
transfer call in a session stored before SMA-810 to directly after the
transfer calls of its handoff response, in call order. A moved result
with the synthetic cancel text gets the transfer text ("transferred to
{target}" for the first transfer call, "transfer not performed: this
response already transferred to {target}" for each other call). No
other result moves, the message count does not change, and the stored
log does not change. A log with no handoff and a new-layout log project
in event order as before.
The cancel text is now the CANCELLED_TOOL_CALL_TEXT const, and
transfer_calls_before shares the boundary scan transfer_run_start.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: ad6d4840c7d6
--- 880b3584 fix(core): SMA-810 let a handoff child defer a call that repeats a transfer call id
Behaviour change (2): a handoff child can now defer a call whose call id
is the same as a transfer call above it (for example `fc_0` from Gemini).
The parent emits the transfer result directly after the handoff, so the
deferral stays open in the session log and a resume can run it. Before
this change, such a call was denied with "permission denied: deferral not
possible: call id {call_id} repeats in this run".
Remove the deny in the `Defer` arm and the `open_call_ids` plumbing of
`RunContext` (both accessors are pub(crate)). Remove the deny text from
the rustdoc of `with_deferred_tool_calls`.
Tests: the runtime-tokio test now defers and resumes the `fc_0` call;
a three-level chain with one call id defers, resumes, and denies on a
renamed root and on a missing middle agent with no new transfer result;
a handoff resume and the resume-route exits add no second transfer result.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 2560adebe2f7
--- 63801a6e fix(core): SMA-810 emit a tool result for each handoff transfer call
Behaviour change (1): a handoff run now emits a ToolOutputItem for each
transfer call, after HandoffItem and before AgentUpdated. The first
transfer call gets "transferred to {target}". Each other transfer call
of the same response gets "transfer not performed: this response already
transferred to {target}". When the target run() returns Err, every
transfer call gets "transfer failed: {target} did not start", then
RunFailed, and no AgentUpdated. A handoff that did not occur (OnHandoff
deny, depth limit, unknown target, swarm max_handoffs) emits no result.
No existing test expectation changed.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
